question: What are the location, shape, and measure of the place described after the recitation stage?
premises: The description applies at the end of the prior stage.
The place is called the three-path place.
It is six-angled and four fingers in measure.
inference: After that stage, attention turns to a six-angled three-path place measuring four fingers.
uncertainties: The exact anatomical or subtle-body referent of tripathasthānaṃ is not specified.
plain_english: At the end of that, there is the three-path place, six-angled and measuring four fingers.
